staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable snapshot, so every source location below is anchored to its exact line map.

classification.classification_note: The saved AddressSanitizer failure is a `container-overflow READ of size 5`, but the source bug is the null-terminated, non-padded boolean parser fast path: it only requires `end - it >= 4` and then unconditionally copies 5 bytes.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 425406132 (glaze): Container-overflow READ 5 found by fuzz target json_generic [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/425406132
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source snapshot
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced AddressSanitizer's `container-overflow READ of size 5` against the staged ARVO checkout `17d81a64b4f8c6824ff119f82cce8419b35791f4`, so this trace is grounded to that source snapshot rather than the metadata vulnerable commit `cf787ad6517ac86f9a3c9719c546757b14fc7a9b`. The exact saved file `gt_results/arvo_425406132/poc` is 14 bytes: `[true,true,tur`. In `json_generic`'s const-input branch, the harness copies those bytes into `std::vector<char> buffer`, appends one `\0`, binds `const auto& input = buffer`, and calls `glz::read_json(json, input)` at line 29. `glz::read` therefore parses a 15-byte `[true,true,tur\0]` buffer with `Opts.null_terminated = true` but `use_padded = false`. The root `json_t` parse enters the array arm, the array loop consumes the first two `true` elements and the second comma, and the third-element cursor lands on the final `t` with `end - it == 4`. In `glz::from<JSON, bool>::op`, the only dynamic length check is `size_t(end - it) < 4`, so the truncated tail `tur\0` passes. The vulnerable null-terminated fast path then assumes it may "read one more index without checking" and executes `std::memcpy(&c, it, 5)`. Only four bytes remain inside the vector's logical range (`t`, `u`, `r`, `\0`), so the fifth byte comes from one byte past the vector size, matching the saved AddressSanitizer crash at `include/glaze/json/read.hpp:543:16`. The fix removes this assumption by copying four bytes first, advancing `it`, and explicitly checking `it == end` before reading the trailing `'e'` of `false`.

constexpr bool use_padded = resizable<Buffer> && non_const_buffer<Buffer> && !check_disable_padding(Opts);
auto [it, end] = read_iterators<Opts, use_padded>(buffer);
source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker buffer into parser padding mode and `it/end` bounds. For the const-input `json_generic` call, this creates the exact active parse span later over-read by the boolean fast path.
source.value_from: The saved `poc` bytes are `5b 74 72 75 65 2c 74 72 75 65 2c 74 75 72` (`[true,true,tur`). `fuzzing/json_generic.cpp` copies them into a `std::vector<char>`, appends one `\0`, and passes a const reference into `glz::read_json`, so this step sees a 15-byte `[true,true,tur\0]` buffer with no extra parser padding.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The 5-byte copy starts at the four-byte tail `tur\0` and reads one byte past the vector's logical end.
sink.note: The saved trace reports `AddressSanitizer: container-overflow READ of size 5` at `/src/glaze/include/glaze/json/read.hpp:543:16`. ASan names address `0x50300000010f`, 15 bytes into the vector allocation created by `buffer.push_back('\0')`, which is exactly the fifth byte of a 5-byte read starting at `buffer.data() + 11`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. In the non-padded boolean parser, the null-terminated fast path assumes a fifth byte is always readable after the 4-byte minimum check. It does not verify `end - it >= 5` or `it != end` before the 5-byte copy.
root_cause.note: The bundled fix rewrites this path to `std::memcpy(&c, it, 4); it += 4;` and then rejects `it == end` before reading the final `'e'`, confirming that the vulnerable code was missing an end-of-buffer obligation for the fifth byte.

tainted_value_origin.description: This comma-handling increment materializes the final-element cursor later passed into the boolean parser. After the second comma in the witness, `it` points at the truncated token `tur` while `end` still points to the appended NUL.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: In `[true,true,tur\0]`, the second comma is at offset 10. `++it` advances the cursor to offset 11 (`'t'`), so `end - it == 4` and the remaining bytes are `74 75 72 00`.

parser_admitted.description: The root `json_t` dispatcher sees the witness's leading `[` and commits to the array parser, which is the only path that can reach the third truncated element after two earlier `true` elements.

evidence_limitations: The staged vulnerable workspace inside the ARVO container is at commit `17d81a64b4f8c6824ff119f82cce8419b35791f4`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `cf787ad6517ac86f9a3c9719c546757b14fc7a9b`. This GT therefore grounds all lines and code snippets to the staged source that Stage 01 actually compiled and crashed on, while retaining the metadata commits as provenance.

fine_trace.note: The exact 14-byte witness becomes a 15-byte vector `[true,true,tur\0]`. The saved ASan stack points to this const-input call at line 29. Passing `input` as const preserves the single appended NUL but prevents `glz::read` from resizing the buffer to add extra SWAR padding.

fine_trace.code:
constexpr bool use_padded = resizable<Buffer> && non_const_buffer<Buffer> && !check_disable_padding(Opts);
auto [it, end] = read_iterators<Opts, use_padded>(buffer);
fine_trace.note: Source. For `Buffer = const std::vector<char>`, `use_padded` is false, so `read_iterators` returns the exact active span `it = buffer.data()`, `end = buffer.data() + 15`. The parser therefore sees only `[true,true,tur\0]`; the byte after the appended NUL is already outside the vector's logical range.
At the root `json_t` parse, `*it == '['`, so the variant dispatcher takes the array arm and commits the witness to the JSON array parser.

The first two loop iterations consume the leading `true` and `true`. After the second comma at byte 10, `++it` advances to byte 11, the third-element start `'t'`; with `end = buffer.data() + 15`, exactly four bytes remain: `tur\0`.
Because the remaining element starts with `'t'`, the `json_t` variant dispatcher selects the boolean parser for the final array element.

The only runtime length check in the non-padded boolean parser rejects tails shorter than 4 bytes. Here `end - it == 4`, so the truncated tail `tur\0` passes this guard instead of failing before the fast-path read.

fine_trace.note: Root cause. After step 5 lets the four-byte tail through, the null-terminated fast path assumes a fifth readable byte exists and performs no `end - it >= 5` or `it != end` check. The fix replaces this assumption with a 4-byte copy plus an explicit end test before reading the fifth character of `false`.

ASan sink. Starting from the four-byte tail `tur\0`, this copies a fifth byte from `buffer.data() + 15`, one byte past the vector's logical end. The saved report names this exact line as `container-overflow READ of size 5` on the const-input stack rooted at `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` line 29.

allocation_context.note: The ASan allocation stack attributes the backing region to the `std::vector<char>` growth triggered by `buffer.push_back('\0')` in the const-input harness path.

poc.trigger: Run the saved 14-byte file through the staged vulnerable `json_generic` target. The const-input branch appends one `\0`, calls `glz::read_json(json, input)` at `fuzzing/json_generic.cpp:29`, and the third array element reaches the boolean fast path as the four-byte tail `tur\0`, which triggers the saved 5-byte container-overflow read.

format.name: truncated JSON array
format.contract: The file must be exactly `[true,true,tur`. Under `json_generic`, the harness appends a single trailing `\0` and passes a const `std::vector<char>` to `glz::read_json`, so the third array element reaches `glz::from<JSON, bool>::op` as `tur\0` with no extra parser padding.
